agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

<output>
# xcp: An extended cp

`xcp` is a (partial) clone of the Unix `cp` command. It is not intended as a
full replacement, but as a companion utility with some more user-friendly
feedback and some optimisations that make sense under certain tasks (see
below).

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/xcp.svg?colorA=777777)](https://crates.io/crates/xcp) 
![Github Actions](https://github.com/tarka/xcp/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)
[![Packaging status](https://repology.org/badge/tiny-repos/xcp.svg)](https://repology.org/project/xcp/versions)

*Warning*: `xcp` is currently beta-level software and almost certainly contains
bugs and unexpected or inconsistent behaviour. It probably shouldn't be used for
anything critical yet.

Please note that there are some known issues with copying files from virtual
filesystems (e.g. `/proc`, `/sys`). See [this LWN
article](https://lwn.net/Articles/846403/) for an overview of some of the
complexities of dealing with kernel-generated files.  This is a common problem
with file utilities which rely on random access; for example `rsync` has the
same issue.

## Installation

### Cargo

`xcp` can be installed directly from `crates.io` with:
```
cargo install xcp
```

### Arch Linux

[`xcp`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/xcp/) is available on the Arch Linux User Repository. If you use an AUR helper, you can execute a command such as this:
```
yay -S xcp
```

### NetBSD
[`xcp`](https://pkgsrc.se/sysutils/xcp) is available on NetBSD from the official repositories. To install it, simply run:
```
pkgin install xcp
```

## Features and Anti-Features

### Features

* Displays a progress-bar, both for directory and single file copies. This can
  be disabled with `--no-progress`.
* On Linux it uses `copy_file_range` call to copy files. This is the most
  efficient method of file-copying under Linux; in particular it is
  filesystem-aware, and can massively speed-up copies on network mounts by
  performing the copy operations server-side. However, unlike `copy_file_range`
  sparse files are detected and handled appropriately.
* Support for modern filesystem features such as [reflinks](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Reflink.html).
* Optimised for 'modern' systems (i.e. multiple cores, copious RAM, and
  solid-state disks, especially ones connected into the main system bus,
  e.g. NVMe).
* Optional aggressive parallelism for systems with parallel IO. Quick
  experiments on a modern laptop suggest there may be benefits to parallel
  copies on NVMe disks. This is obviously highly system-dependent.
* Switchable 'drivers' to facilitate experimenting with alternative strategies
  for copy optimisation. Currently 2 drivers are available:
  * 'parfile': the previous hard-coded xcp copy method, which parallelises
    tree-walking and per-file copying. This is the default.
  * 'parblock': An experimental driver that parallelises copying at the block
    level. This has the potential for performance improvements in some
    architectures, but increases complexity. Testing is welcome.
* Non-Linux Unix-like OSs (OS X, *BSD) are supported via fall-back operation
  (although sparse-files are not yet supported in this case).
* Optionally understands `.gitignore` files to limit the copied directories.
* Optional native file-globbing.

### (Possible) future features

* Conversion of files to sparse where appropriate, as with `cp`'s
  `--sparse=always` flag.
* Aggressive sparseness detection with `lseek`.
* On non-Linux OSs sparse-files are not currenty supported but could be added if
  supported by the OS.

### Differences with `cp`

* Permissions, xattrs and ACLs are copied by default; this can be disabled with
  `--no-perms`.
* Virtual file copies are not supported; for example `/proc` and `/sys` files.
* Character files such as [sockets](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html) and
  [pipes](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/mkfifo.3.html) are copied as
  devices (i.e. via [mknod](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/mknod.2.html))
  rather than copying their contents as a stream.
* The `--reflink=never` option may silently perform a reflink operation
  regardless. This is due to the use of
  [copy_file_range](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/copy_file_range.2.html)
  which has no such override and may perform its own optimisations.
* `cp` 'simple' backups are not supported, only numbered.
* Some `cp` options are not available but may be added in the future.

## Performance

Benchmarks are mostly meaningless, but the following are results from a laptop
with an NVMe disk and in single-user mode. The target copy directory is a git
checkout of the Firefox codebase, having been recently gc'd (i.e. a single 4.1GB
pack file). `fstrim -va` and `echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` are
run before each test run to minimise SSD allocation performance interference.

Note: `xcp` is optimised for 'modern' systems with lots of RAM and solid-state
disks. In particular it is likely to perform worse on spinning disks unless they
are in highly parallel arrays.

### Local copy

* Single 4.1GB file copy, with the kernel cache dropped each run:
    * `cp`: ~6.2s
    * `xcp`: ~4.2s
* Single 4.1GB file copy, warmed cache (3 runs each):
    * `cp`: ~1.85s
    * `xcp`: ~1.7s
* Directory copy, kernel cache dropped each run:
    * `cp`: ~48s
    * `xcp`: ~56s
* Directory copy, warmed cache (3 runs each):
    * `cp`: ~6.9s
    * `xcp`: ~7.4s

### NFS copy

`xcp` uses `copy_file_range`, which is filesystem aware. On NFSv4 this will result
in the copy occurring server-side rather than transferring across the network. For
large files this can be a significant win:

* Single 4.1GB file on NFSv4 mount
    * `cp`: 6m18s
    * `xcp`: 0m37s

### AI Contribution Policy

This project will not accept runtime code generated by AI. Generation of _draft_
documentation and test code is acceptable, but should be reviewed by the
submitter before raising a PR.

# test sparse files? maybe relevant

rm -rf /tmp/testxcp; mkdir -p /tmp/testxcp/src /tmp/testxcp/dest

ls -l /tmp/testxcp/dest/a

echo data > /tmp/testxcp/src/a
# driver aliases file-parallel and block-parallel?

for d in parfile parblock file-parallel block-parallel file_parallel block_parallel par-file par-block; do
  echo -n "$d: "
  ./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --driver $d -v 2>&1 | tail -n 1; echo ec ${PIPESTATUS[0]}; rm -f /tmp/testxcp/dest/a
done

# check reflink values
for r in auto always never off none; do
  echo -n "reflink $r: "
  ./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --reflink $r -v 2>&1 | tail -n 1; echo ec ${PIPESTATUS[0]}; rm -f /tmp/testxcp/dest/a
done

# backup
for b in none off numbered auto simple; do
  echo -n "backup $b: "
  ./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --backup $b -v 2>&1 | tail -n 2; echo ec ${PIPESTATUS[0]}; rm -f /tmp/testxcp/dest/a
done

# check block-size parsing case insensitivity
for sz in 1kb 1KB 1k 1K 1m 1M 1mb 1MB 1MiB 1mib 1g 1G 1GiB 1b 512B 1kB; do
  echo -n "$sz: "
  ./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --block-size $sz -v 2>&1 | tail -n 1
  echo ec ${PIPESTATUS[0]}; rm -f /tmp/testxcp/dest/a
done

# check ownership copies?
# check xattrs? Probably copies.

# check error messages exact formatting
./executable /nonexistent /tmp --no-progress 2>&1
./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a /tmp/testxcp/src/a --no-progress 2>&1
./executable -r /tmp/testxcp/src /tmp/testxcp/src --no-progress 2>&1

# check self copy directory into itself detection: same path vs subdir?
mkdir -p /tmp/testxcp/src/sub
./executable -r /tmp/testxcp/src /tmp/testxcp/src/sub --no-progress 2>&1; echo ec $?
./executable -r /tmp/testxcp/src /tmp/testxcp/src/sub/sub2 --no-progress 2>&1; echo ec $?

# check target-directory existence
rm -rf /tmp/testxcp/dest/target; mkdir -p /tmp/testxcp/dest/target
./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a --target-directory /tmp/testxcp/dest/target/notexist --no-progress -v 2>&1; echo ec $?

# check when dest dir does not exist and we copy multiple sources to non-existing target-directory? Actually target-directory flag overrides.

# check verbose count 0 = no info?
./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress 2>&1; echo ec $?
# with -v prints info
# with -vv debug?
./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress -vv 2>&1 | head

# check fsync, no-perms, no-timestamps interplay
rm /tmp/testxcp/dest/a
./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --fsync --no-perms --no-timestamps -v 2>&1

# check .gitignore only root?
rm -rf /tmp/testxcp/src /tmp/testxcp/dest; mkdir -p /tmp/testxcp/src/sub
echo hello > /tmp/testxcp/src/a.txt
echo subfile > /tmp/testxcp/src/sub/b.txt
echo "*.log" > /tmp/testxcp/src/.gitignore
echo ignore.log > /tmp/testxcp/src/ignore.log
echo also.log > /tmp/testxcp/src/sub/also.log
./executable -r /tmp/testxcp/src /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --gitignore -v 2>&1; ls -R /tmp/testxcp/dest

# check glob with recursive?
rm -rf /tmp/testxcp/dest/*; mkdir -p /tmp/testxcp/src/dir
echo f1 > /tmp/testxcp/src/dir/f1.txt
./executable -g -r --no-progress "/tmp/testxcp/src/*" /tmp/testxcp/dest -v 2>&1; ls -R /tmp/testxcp/dest

# check hidden files: does gitignore cause .gitignore file itself to be copied? earlier test showed .gitignore copied even with --gitignore. Let's see implementation: it should copy .gitignore itself
rm -rf /tmp/testxcp/dest; mkdir /tmp/testxcp/dest
./executable -r /tmp/testxcp/src /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --gitignore -v 2>&1; ls -la /tmp/testxcp/dest; cat /tmp/testxcp/dest/.gitignore 2>&1 || echo no gitignore

# check backup auto logic when previous backups exist: we saw earlier it created ~2~ when ~1~ existed. Need to test more.
rm -rf /tmp/testxcp; mkdir -p /tmp/testxcp/src /tmp/testxcp/dest
echo orig > /tmp/testxcp/dest/a.txt

./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a.txt /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --backup auto -v 2>&1; ls -l /tmp/testxcp/dest
cat /tmp/testxcp/dest/a.txt
# now numbered
rm -f /tmp/testxcp/dest/a.txt.~2~; echo new2 > /tmp/testxcp/src/a.txt
./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a.txt /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --backup numbered -v 2>&1; ls -l /tmp/testxcp/dest
# off
./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a.txt /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress --backup off -v 2>&1; ls -l /tmp/testxcp/dest

# test ownership warning if not root? -o should warn?
./executable /tmp/testxcp/src/a.txt /tmp/testxcp/dest --no-progress -o -v 2>&1; echo ec $?
"}

build = false
include = [
    "build.rs",
    "src/**/*",
    "Cargo.toml",
    "LICENSE*",
    "README.md",
    "examples/**/*",
]
autolib = false
autobins = false
autoexamples = false
autotests = false
autobenches = false
description = "A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser"
readme = "README.md"
keywords = [
    "argument",
    "cli",
    "arg",
    "parser",
    "parse",
]
categories = ["command-line-interface"]
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/clap-rs/clap"
resolver = "2"

[package.metadata.docs.rs]
features = ["unstable-doc"]
rustdoc-args = ["--generate-link-to-definition"]

[package.metadata.playground]
features = ["unstable-doc"]

[package.metadata.release]
shared-version = true
dependent-version = "upgrade"
tag-name = "v{{version}}"

[features]
cargo = []
color = ["dep:anstream"]
debug = ["dep:backtrace"]
default = [
    "std",
    "color",
    "help",
    "usage",
    "error-context",
    "suggestions",
]
deprecated = []
env = []
error-context = []
help = []
std = ["anstyle/std"]
string = []
suggestions = [
    "dep:strsim",
    "error-context",
]
unicode = [
    "dep:unicode-width",
    "dep:unicase",
]
unstable-doc = [
    "cargo",
    "wrap_help",
    "env",
    "unicode",
    "string",
    "unstable-ext",
]
unstable-ext = []
unstable-styles = ["color"]
unstable-v5 = ["deprecated"]
usage = []
wrap_help = [
    "help",
    "dep:terminal_size",
]

[lib]
</output>

        .arg(Arg::new("glob").short('g').long("glob").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Expand file patterns.\n\nGlob (expand) filename patterns natively (note; the shell may still do its own expansion first)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-progress").long("no-progress").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Disable progress bar"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-perms").long("no-perms").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Do not copy the file permissions"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-timestamps").long("no-timestamps").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Do not copy the file timestamps"))
        .arg(Arg::new("ownership").short('o').long("ownership").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Copy ownership.\n\nWhether to copy ownship (user/group).         .arg(Arg::new("no-target-directory").short('T').long("no-target-directory").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Target should not be a directory.\n\nAnalogous to cp's no-target-directory.         .arg(Arg::new("target-directory").long("target-directory").help("Copy into a subdirectory of the target"))

mod filetime {
    use std::path::Path;
    use std::fs::Metadata;
    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
    #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
    pub struct FileTime { secs: i64, nsecs: i32 }
    impl FileTime {
        pub fn from_last_access_time(meta: &Metadata) -> Self {
            let atime = meta.accessed().unwrap_or(SystemTime::now());
            let dur = atime.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default();
            Self { secs: dur.as_secs() as i64, nsecs: dur.subsec_nanos() as i32 }
        }
        pub fn from_last_modification_time(meta: &Metadata) -> Self {
            let mtime = meta.modified().unwrap_or(SystemTime::now());
            let dur = mtime.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default();
            Self { secs: dur.as_secs() as i64, nsecs: dur.subsec_nanos() as i32 }
        }
    }
    pub fn set_file_times(path: &Path, atime: FileTime, mtime: FileTime) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        let atime_tv = libc::timeval { tv_sec: atime.secs as _, tv_usec: (atime.nsecs/1000) as _ };
        let mtime_tv = libc::timeval { tv_sec: mtime.secs as _, tv_usec: (mtime.nsecs/1000) as _ };
        let times = [atime_tv, mtime_tv];
        let c_path = std::ffi::CString::new(path.to_string_lossy().as_bytes()).unwrap();
        let ret = unsafe { libc::utimes(c_path.as_ptr(), times.as_ptr()) };
        if ret==0 { Ok(()) } else { Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error()) }
    }
}

fn handle_backup(dst: &Path, backup: Backup, verbose: u8) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    if !dst.exists() { return Ok(()); }
    match backup {
        Backup::None | Backup::Off => Ok(()),
        Backup::Numbered => {
            let parent = dst.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new("."));
            let file_name = dst.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().to_string();
            let mut max_num = 0;
            if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(parent) {
                for entry in entries {
                    if let Ok(entry) = entry {
                        let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
                        if name.starts_with(&format!("{}.~", file_name)) && name.ends_with('~') {
                            let inner = &name[file_name.len()+2..name.len()-1];
                            if let Ok(n) = inner.parse::<u64>() {
                                if n > max_num { max_num = n; }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            let next = max_num + 1;
            let backup_name = format!("{}.~{}~", file_name, next);
            let backup_path = parent.join(backup_name);
            if verbose >= 1 {
                println!("{} Backup: Rename {:?} to {:?}", format_log("INFO"), dst, backup_path);
            }
            fs::rename(dst, backup_path)?;
            Ok(())
        },
        Backup::Auto => {
            let parent = dst.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new("."));
            let file_name = dst.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().to_string();
            let mut has_backup = false;
            let mut max_num = 0;
            if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(parent) {
                for entry in entries {
                    if let Ok(entry) = entry {
                        let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
                        if name.starts_with(&format!("{}.~", file_name)) && name.ends_with('~') {
                            has_backup = true;
                            let inner = &name[file_name.len()+2..name.len()-1];
                            if let Ok(n) = inner.parse::<u64>() {
                                if n > max_num { max_num = n; }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            if !has_backup { return Ok(()); }
            let next = max_num + 1;
            let backup_name = format!("{}.~{}~", file_name, next);
            let backup_path = parent.join(backup_name);
            if verbose >= 1 {
                println!("{} Backup: Rename {:?} to {:?}", format_log("INFO"), dst, backup_path);
            }
            fs::rename(dst, backup_path)?;
            Ok(())
        }
    }
}

./executable.new /tmp/t/src/a /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --backup auto -v
ls /tmp/t/dest/a.~2~

echo "Testing reflink never warning"

./executable.new /tmp/t/src/a /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --reflink never > /tmp/out 2>&1
cat /tmp/out | grep "WARN" || (echo "no warn"; exit 1)

ls /tmp/t/dest/a

./executable.new -r /tmp/t/src /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --gitignore -v
ls /tmp/t/dest/a.txt && ls /tmp/t/dest/sub/b.txt && [ ! -f /tmp/t/dest/ignore.log ] && echo "gitignore ok" || (echo "gitignore fail"; exit 1)

./executable.new -g "/tmp/t/src/*.txt" /tmp/t/dest --no-progress -v

rm -rf /tmp/t; mkdir -p /tmp/t/src /tmp/t/target; echo hi > /tmp/t/src/a
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/a --target-directory /tmp/t/target --no-progress -v
ls /tmp/t/target/a

rm -rf /tmp/t; mkdir -p /tmp/t/src/sub /tmp/t/dest; echo f > /tmp/t/src/sub/f
./executable.new -r -T /tmp/t/src /tmp/t/dest --no-progress -v

echo "Testing block-size parsing"

./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --block-size 1KB -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --block-size invalid 2>&1 | grep "invalid value" || (echo "block-size fail"; exit 1)

./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --driver parfile -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --driver parblock -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --driver invalid 2>&1 | grep "Unknown driver" || (echo "driver fail"; exit 1)

echo "Testing reflink parsing"
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --reflink auto -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --reflink always -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --reflink never -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --reflink invalid 2>&1 | grep "Unexpected value" || (echo "reflink fail"; exit 1)

echo "Testing backup parsing"
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --backup none -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --backup off -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/v/dest --no-progress --backup numbered -v || true
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --backup auto -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --backup invalid 2>&1 | grep "Unexpected value" || (echo "backup fail"; exit 1)

echo "Testing workers"
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --workers 0 -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --workers 1 -v
./executable.new /tmp/t/src/sub/f /tmp/t/dest --no-progress --workers invalid 2>&1 | grep "invalid digit" || (echo "workers fail"; exit 1)

SH

/tmp/run_final.sh 2>&1 | tail -n 100

# In clap_builder, short help is shown when -h, long help when --help. If we provide both help and long_help, -h shows help, --help shows long_help.
# Our current code uses help with long paragraphs, so both -h and --help show same long. We need to make help short, long_help long.

# Let's adjust build_cli to use help for short and long_help for long where needed.

cat <<'PY' > /tmp/patch_help.py
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('src/main.rs')
s=p.read_text()

# Define a helper to replace Arg definitions to have both help and long_help
# We'll replace build_cli function with version that uses help and long_help appropriately

new_build_cli = """fn build_cli() -> clap::ArgMatches {
    Command::new("executable")
        .about("A (partial) clone of the Unix `cp` command with progress and pluggable drivers.")
        .version("0.24.3")
        .arg(Arg::new("verbose").short('v').long("verbose").action(ArgAction::Count).help("Verbosity").long_help("Verbosity.\\n\\nCan be specified multiple times to increase logging."))
        .arg(Arg::new("recursive").short('r').long("recursive").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Copy directories recursively"))
        .arg(Arg::new("dereference").short('L').long("dereference").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Dereference symlinks in source").long_help("Dereference symlinks in source\\n\\nFollow symlinks, possibly recursively, when copying source files."))
        .arg(Arg::new("workers").short('w').long("workers").default_value("4").help("Number of parallel workers").long_help("Number of parallel workers.\\n\\nDefault is 4; if the value is negative or 0 it uses the number of logical CPUs.\\n\\n[default: 4]").value_name("WORKERS"))
        .arg(Arg::new("block-size").long("block-size").default_value("1MB").help("Block size for operations").long_help("Block size for operations.\\n\\nAccepts standard size modifiers like \\\"M\\\" and \\\"GB\\\". Actual usage internally depends on the driver.\\n\\n[default: 1MB]").value_name("BLOCK_SIZE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-clobber").short('n').long("no-clobber").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Do not overwrite an existing file"))
        .arg(Arg::new("force").short('f').long("force").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Force (compatability only)").long_help("Force (compatability only)\\n\\nOverwrite files; this is the default behaviour, this flag is for compatibility with `cp` only. See `--no-clobber` for the inverse flag. Using this in conjunction with `--no-clobber` will cause an error."))
        .arg(Arg::new("gitignore").long("gitignore").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Use .gitignore if present").long_help("Use .gitignore if present.\\n\\nNOTE: This is fairly basic at the moment, and only honours a .gitignore in the directory root for directory copies; global or sub-directory ignores are skipped."))
        .arg(Arg::new("glob").short('g').long("glob").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Expand file patterns").long_help("Expand file patterns.\\n\\nGlob (expand) filename patterns natively (note; the shell may still do its own expansion first)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-progress").long("no-progress").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Disable progress bar"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-perms").long("no-perms").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Do not copy the file permissions"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-timestamps").long("no-timestamps").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Do not copy the file timestamps"))
        .arg(Arg::new("ownership").short('o').long("ownership").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Copy ownership").long_help("Copy ownership.\\n\\nWhether to copy ownship (user/group).  This option requires root permissions or appropriate capabilities; if the attempt to copy ownership fails a warning is issued but the operation continues."))
        .arg(Arg::new("driver").long("driver").default_value("parfile").help("Driver to use, defaults to 'file-parallel'").long_help("Driver to use, defaults to 'file-parallel'.\\n\\nCurrently there are 2; the default \\\"parfile\\\", which parallelises copies across workers at the file level, and an experimental \\\"parblock\\\" driver, which parellelises at the block level. See also '--block-size'.\\n\\n[default: parfile]").value_name("DRIVER"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-target-directory").short('T').long("no-target-directory").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Target should not be a directory").long_help("Target should not be a directory.\\n\\nAnalogous to cp's no-target-directory. Expected behavior is that when copying a directory to another directory, instead of creating a sub-folder in target, overwrite target."))
        .arg(Arg::new("target-directory").long("target-directory").value_name("TARGET_DIRECTORY").help("Copy into a subdirectory of the target"))
        .arg(Arg::new("fsync").long("fsync").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Sync each file to disk after writing"))
        .arg(Arg::new("reflink").long("reflink").default_value("auto").help("Reflink options").long_help("Reflink options.\\n\\nWhether and how to use reflinks. 'auto' (the default) will attempt to reflink and fallback to a copy if it is not possible, 'always' will return an error if it cannot reflink, and 'never' will always perform a full data copy.\\n\\nNote: when using Linux accelerated copy operations (the default when available) the kernel may choose to reflink rather than perform a fully copy regardless of this setting.\\n\\n[default: auto]").value_name("REFLINK"))
        .arg(Arg::new("backup").long("backup").default_value("none").help("Backup options").long_help("Backup options\\n\\nWhether to create backups of overwritten files. Current options are 'none'/'off', or 'numbered', or 'auto'. Numbered backups follow the semantics of `cp` numbered backups (e.g. `file.txt.~123~`). 'auto' will only create a numbered backup if a previous backups exists. Default is 'none'.\\n\\n[default: none]").value_name("BACKUP"))
        .arg(Arg::new("paths").value_name("PATHS").num_args(0..).help("Path list").long_help("Path list.\\n\\nSource and destination files, or multiple source(s) to a directory."))
        .get_matches()
}
"""

# Replace old build_cli
import re
pattern = r"fn build_cli\(\) -> clap::ArgMatches \{.*?\.get_matches\(\)\n\}"
m = re.search(pattern, s, re.DOTALL)
if not m:
    print("not found build_cli")
    # try alternative
    # Find function start
    idx = s.find("fn build_cli()")
    # find next "\n}\n\nfn format_log"
    idx2 = s.find("\n}\n\nfn format_log", idx)
    if idx2 != -1:
        old = s[idx:idx2+2]
        s = s.replace(old, new_build_cli+"\n\n")
        print("replaced via manual")
    else:
        print("failed")
else:
    old = m.group(0)
    s = s.replace(old, new_build_cli)
    print("replaced via regex")

p.write_text(s)
PY
python3 /tmp/patch_help.py
cargo build --offline --release 2>&1 | tail -n 20
